nodes.name: Hydrocyclone Classifier
nodes.definition: A centrifugal hydraulic classifier used to separate slurry into coarse and fine fractions by particle size and density. In flotation preparation circuits it is applied for classification and slime removal prior to conditioning and flotation.

nodes.name: Rod Mill
nodes.definition: A grinding mill that uses long steel rods as the grinding media, suitable for coarse grinding and achieving a relatively narrow product size distribution. In gold ore processing, it is often used in the first grinding stage; at the Cannon plant it feeds a carbon flotation section.

nodes.name: Two-Chamber Jigging Machine
nodes.definition: A gravity concentration device with two compartments used to recover native copper from the grinding circuit discharge before flotation. Installed at the Horseshoe plant to capture coarse copper particles and prevent cyanicide losses.

nodes.name: Pyrrhotite-Bearing Gold Ore
nodes.definition: Gold ore containing pyrrhotite, which consumes oxygen and cyanide during cyanidation, generates acidity, and produces thiosulfate and other sulfur species that can inhibit gold dissolution. These ores often require pre-aeration or oxidative roasting.

nodes.name: Chalcopyrite
nodes.definition: Copper iron sulfide mineral referenced as weakly affected by copper sulfate treatment. Its surface state strongly influences collector adsorption and flotation behavior.

nodes.name: Hydrogen Peroxide
nodes.definition: An oxidizing reagent used to pre-oxidize sulfide concentrates before selective flotation. In the slice it is especially effective in combination with dichromate for separating cinnabar from stibnite.

nodes.name: Desorption Temperature 90тАп┬░C
nodes.definition: Operating temperature for hot caustic cyanide elution of loaded activated carbon. At 90тАп┬░C with 10тАпg/L NaOH and 2тАпg/L NaCN, gold is desorbed to residual <155тАпg/t in a 60тАСhour circulation cycle.

nodes.name: Gold Grade
nodes.definition: Mass concentration of gold in ore, usually expressed in grams per ton. It is the key technical indicator used to assess ore quality and to compare the economic attractiveness of placer and lode deposits.

nodes.name: Overall Gold Recovery
nodes.definition: The fraction of gold in the mined ore that is transferred into the final product, integrating all beneficiation stages. In the slice, the Itogon plant achieved 86.8% overall recovery from a pyritic ore.
nodes.text: Overall Gold Recovery (╨╛╨▒╤Й╨╡╨╡ ╨╕╨╖╨▓╨╗╨╡╤З╨╡╨╜╨╕╨╡ ╨╖╨╛╨╗╨╛╤В╨░, overall gold extraction)

nodes.name: Steel Rod Consumption
nodes.definition: Mass of grinding rods consumed per ton of ore or concentrate in a rod mill. At the Getchell plant (historical, 1960s) consumption was 0.54тАпkg/t of ore.

nodes.name: Native Gold
nodes.definition: Natural metallic gold, the primary valuable mineral. Density 15.6тАУ18.3 g/cm┬│, hardness 2тАУ3, malleable, non-magnetic. Not directly depressing but its surface may be passivated by associated minerals.

nodes.name: Native Silver
nodes.definition: Natural metallic silver. Density 10.1тАУ11.1 g/cm┬│, hardness 2.5тАУ3, very malleable, non-magnetic, conductive.

nodes.name: Sphalerite
nodes.definition: Zinc sulfide mineral whose flotation properties can be significantly altered by copper sulfate activation. It is a key sulfide mineral in selective flotation circuits.

nodes.name: Limonite
nodes.definition: Hydrated iron oxide mineral, a common weathering product. Causes physical depression of gold and silver during cyanidation. Density 3.3тАУ4.0 g/cm┬│, hardness 4тАУ5, brittle, moderately magnetic.

nodes.name: Native Copper
nodes.definition: Naturally occurring metallic copper that occurs in some oxidized copper-gold ores. It is recovered by gravity concentration before flotation to prevent excessive cyanide consumption and to improve overall copper recovery.

nodes.name: Chrysocolla
nodes.definition: Hydrated copper silicate mineral included among oxidized copper-bearing minerals. It is important in flotation because its surface is strongly hydrated and often requires special treatment for recovery.

nodes.name: Malachite
nodes.definition: A copper carbonate mineral mentioned as being activated by very small doses of sodium silicate in flotation. It is relevant as an oxide/carbonate copper mineral whose surface chemistry can change markedly under regulator treatment.

nodes.name: Azurite
nodes.definition: Copper carbonate mineral included among oxidized copper minerals. It is important in flotation as an example of a hydrophilic oxidized phase that requires specialized collectors or activation.

nodes.name: Iron Hydroxides
nodes.definition: Insoluble iron-containing precipitates formed when iron ions are removed from solution by alkali addition. In flotation, iron hydroxides are used to suppress unwanted iron-ion activation and to reduce the adverse influence of dissolved iron species on reagent selectivity.

nodes.name: Amyl Xanthate
nodes.definition: Higher-chain xanthate collector used for sulfide mineral flotation. The slice shows that its performance can be further improved by combining it with dithiophosphate, although the synergy depends on reagent ratio and mineral surface state.

nodes.name: S-4037 Collector
nodes.definition: Synthetic organic flotation collector reagent (type S-4037) used in copper-gold flotation circuits. Added as a supplementary collector to improve recovery of copper and gold, typically dosed at 0.02 kg/t of ore.

nodes.name: Methyl Isobutyl Carbinol
nodes.definition: A secondary alcohol widely used as a high-efficiency frother in ore and coal flotation. The text emphasizes its high selectivity and its positive effect on concentrate quality and recovery.

nodes.name: Aeroflot-N
nodes.definition: A type of dithiophosphate flotation collector (aerofloat) used in selective flotation of copper-gold ores. Applied at a rate of 20 g/t in alkaline pH (9.4тАУ9.6) at the Oiankos plant to hydrophobize sulfide minerals.

nodes.name: Aeroxanthate 301
nodes.definition: A commercial xanthate-based flotation collector (type 301) used for bulk or selective flotation of copper and gold sulfides. Dosed at 60 g/t at the Oiankos plant as part of the collector suite.

nodes.name: Aeroflot 208
nodes.definition: A dithiophosphate flotation collector (aerofloat 208) used in copper-gold flotation. Applied at 60 g/t in the Oiankos flowsheet to enhance recovery of copper and gold minerals.

nodes.name: Marcy Ball Mill
nodes.definition: A brand of ball mill (size 2.74├Ч3.66 m) used for grinding copper-gold ore to flotation feed fineness (70тАУ75 % passing 0.074 mm). Two such mills are used in parallel for gold and gold-copper ore circuits at the Horseshoe plant.
nodes.text: Marcy Ball Mill (╤И╨░╤А╨╛╨▓╨░╤П ╨╝╨╡╨╗╤М╨╜╨╕╤Ж╨░ тАЬ╨Ь╨░╤А╤Б╨╕тАЭ, Marcy mill, ╨╝╨╡╨╗╤М╨╜╨╕╤Ж╨░ ╨Ь╨░╤А╤Б╨╕)

nodes.name: Maxwell Flotation Cell
nodes.definition: Large-volume flotation cell (20тАУ60 m┬│) used in the rougher flotation of gold-copper ores at Canadian plants such as Pamour Porcupine and Copper Rand. It is characterized by low energy consumption and simplified maintenance.
nodes.text: Maxwell Flotation Cell (╨╝╨░╤И╨╕╨╜╨░ ╨Ь╨░╨║╤Б╨▓╨╡╨╗╨╗╨░, MX-10, MX-12, MX-14, Maxwell cell)

nodes.name: Thickener
nodes.definition: A settling vessel used to separate gold-bearing solution from the solid part of the pulp after cyanidation. The overflow is sent for gold recovery, and the underflow is further processed.

nodes.name: Lasta Automatic Filter Press
nodes.definition: Automatic chamber filter press with 22 chambers and 77 m┬▓ total filtration area, used to dewater flotation concentrate. Achieves 8 % cake moisture and reduced operating costs by 26тАп000 USD per month at the Copper Rand plant.
nodes.text: Lasta Automatic Filter Press (╨░╨▓╤В╨╛╨╝╨░╤В╨╕╤З╨╡╤Б╨║╨╕╨╣ ╤Д╨╕╨╗╤М╤В╤А-╨┐╤А╨╡╤Б╤Б тАЬ╨Ы╨░╤Б╤В╨░тАЭ, Lasta filter press, ╤Д╨╕╨╗╤М╤В╤А-╨┐╤А╨╡╤Б╤Б ╨Ы╨░╤Б╤В╨░)

nodes.name: Fagergren Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: Widely used chamber-type flotation machine with a rod rotor-stator aeration system. It provides high pulp aeration at low specific energy consumption and can operate with low pulp depth while maintaining effective froth removal.

nodes.name: Agitair-48 Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: A pneumatic-mechanical flotation machine with forced air supply and mechanical agitation, used for flotation of low-sulfide and oxidized ores at plants like Horoshu and Yellow Pine. It allows independent control of aeration intensity.
nodes.text: Agitair-48 Flotation Machine (╨Р╨┤╨╢╨╕╤В╨╡╨╣╨╡╤А-48, Agitair 48, Agitair flotation cell)

nodes.name: Disc Vacuum Filter
nodes.definition: Continuous vacuum filter constructed from disc-shaped filtration elements operating under vacuum. It belongs to the class of vacuum filters used for granular pulps and offers high filtration area per unit footprint.

nodes.name: Hammer Crusher
nodes.definition: A sizeтАСreduction machine in which material is broken by impact from rapidly rotating hammers. Used for secondary or tertiary crushing of mediumтАСhard and friable ores before grinding. Referenced in the Berengela plant flowsheet for comminution of roasted calcine.

nodes.name: Column Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: Pneumatic flotation machine with a chamber in the form of a column. The slice lists it as one of the main machine configurations used for air introduction and separation.

nodes.name: Froth Flotation
nodes.definition: Modern flotation scheme in which air bubbles, collectors, and frothers are used to transport hydrophobic particles into a stable froth layer. It enabled economically viable and selective separation of fine and polymetallic ores.

nodes.name: Selective Flotation
nodes.definition: Flotation mode designed to separate multiple valuable minerals into individual concentrates. It relies on finely tuned reagent chemistry and differences in surface selectivity.

nodes.name: Staged Flotation
nodes.definition: A flotation flowsheet organized as alternating grinding and flotation stages. This arrangement extracts liberated mineral particles progressively as intergrowths are broken down.

nodes.name: Grinding in Cyanide Solution
nodes.definition: A hydrometallurgical intensification method in which ore is ground in the presence of cyanide solution rather than in water. This initiates gold and silver leaching during comminution, shortens overall cyanidation residence time, allows efficient internal recycling of barren solutions, and can reduce total cyanide consumption.

nodes.name: Multi-Chamber Mechanical Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: A flotation machine consisting of several mechanically agitated chambers arranged in series, used for continuous countercurrent sorption-flotation processes. It is employed to recover loaded powdered activated carbon from cyanide or thiocarbamide pulps.

nodes.name: Autogenous Mill
nodes.definition: Grinding mill in which the ore itself serves as the grinding media without added steel balls or rods. It is used for coarse size reduction in a single stage, reducing steel consumption and wear, but requires competent ore for effective grinding.

nodes.name: Copper Concentrate Grade
nodes.definition: The mass fraction of copper in a flotation concentrate, typically expressed as percent or in decimal form. The text notes that highтАСquality concentrates from segregation roasting can reach 40тАУ60 % copper.

nodes.name: Cake Moisture
nodes.definition: Residual water content retained in the filter cake after filtration. The slice notes that flocculating additives such as polyacrylamide can increase cake moisture because of water retained inside flocs, even while they improve filtration rate.

nodes.name: Granulometric Composition
nodes.definition: Particle-size distribution of the solid phase in an ore or pulp. It strongly affects mixing, slime formation, conditioning behavior, and the flotation response of the feed.

nodes.name: Collector Cost
nodes.definition: Economic indicator describing the cost of flotation collectors per unit mass or process unit. The slice states that apolar collectors are several times cheaper than ionogenic reagents, making collector cost a key driver for reagent selection and process economics.

nodes.name: Closed Circuit
nodes.definition: A processing configuration in which intermediate products are returned to the initial flotation cycles for reprocessing. It is preferred when the recycle stream does not negatively affect pulp conditions or separation efficiency.

nodes.name: Opemiska Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: Canadian gold-copper processing plant owned by Falconbridge, operating since 1963 at 2тАп540тАУ2тАп700 t/d. Processes ore averaging 2.8 g/t Au, 8.7 g/t Ag, 1.16 % Cu with flotation to produce a concentrate for the Noranda smelter. Gold recovery 89.6 %.
nodes.text: Opemiska Plant (Canada) (╤Д╨░╨▒╤А╨╕╨║╨░ ╨Ю╨┐╨╡╨╝╨╕╤Б╨║╨░ (╨Ъ╨░╨╜╨░╨┤╨░), Opemiska concentrator, Falconbridge Opemiska)

nodes.name: Horseshoe Plant (Australia)
nodes.definition: Australian gold-copper processing plant (commissioned 1984) treating gold ores by direct cyanidation/CIP (400 t/d) and gold-copper ores by gravity-flotation (700 t/d). Gold-copper ore grade: 3.9 g/t Au, 35 g/t Ag, 4.1 % Cu. Uses sequential sulfide-oxide flotation with 16 Agitair cells.
nodes.text: Horseshoe Plant (Australia) (╤Д╨░╨▒╤А╨╕╨║╨░ ╨е╨╛╤А╤Б╤И╤Г (╨Р╨▓╤Б╤В╤А╨░╨╗╨╕╤П), Horseshoe concentrator, Horoshu plant)

nodes.name: Oiankos Plant (Chile)
nodes.definition: Chilean gold-copper processing plant (300 t/d) treating mixed sulfide-oxidized ores from several deposits. Ore contains 11тАУ14 g/t Au, 0.6тАУ1.4 % Cu with chalcopyrite, chrysocolla, malachite, azurite, atacamite, and native copper. Uses sequential flotation with aeroflot reagents at pH 9.4тАУ9.6 and grinding in weak cyanide solution.
nodes.text: Oiankos Plant (Chile) (╤Д╨░╨▒╤А╨╕╨║╨░ ╨Ю╤П╨╜╨║╨╛╤Б (╨з╨╕╨╗╨╕), Oiancos concentrator, Oiancos plant)

nodes.name: Chalcocite
nodes.definition: Copper sulfide mineral that can form as a secondary surface phase during mineral alteration. In flotation, it is relevant because it can coat primary sulfides and change their collector response.

nodes.name: Bornite
nodes.definition: A copper iron sulfide mineral (Cu5FeS4) commonly associated with gold in copper-gold ores. It is a significant copper mineral that can be recovered by flotation and, in the context of the slice, appears in synthetic mixtures studied for combined flotation-thiocarbamide leaching.
nodes.text: Bornite (Cu3FeS4, Cu5FeS4, copper iron sulfide, peacock ore, ╨▒╨╛╤А╨╜╨╕╤В)

nodes.name: Sericite
nodes.definition: A fine-grained muscovite mica mineral commonly occurring in alteration zones of gold-antimony ores. Its presence in high content complicates flotation by causing slime interference and requiring staged grinding and desliming operations.

nodes.name: Feldspar
nodes.definition: Rock-forming aluminosilicate mineral that is commonly separated from quartz, kaolin, and mica by flotation. The slice cites feldspar in multiple cationic-collector separation examples.

nodes.name: Intensive Cyanidation
nodes.definition: A short but high-intensity cyanidation process followed by rapid separation of the gold-bearing solution from the pulp or by sorption of the metal from the pulp using synthetic granular sorbents. It is used to minimize gold adsorption by carbonaceous matter.

nodes.name: Regrinding
nodes.definition: Additional grinding applied to concentrates, tailings, or intermediate products after an initial flotation pass. It is used to increase liberation before further flotation or separation.

nodes.name: Gravity Concentrate Upgrading
nodes.definition: A finishing operation for gravity concentrates that removes remaining gangue and sulfides to produce a high-grade product suitable for direct smelting or refining. It typically uses tabling, magnetic separation, or intensive cyanidation.
nodes.text: Gravity Concentrate Upgrading (╨│╨╗╤Г╨▒╨╛╨║╨░╤П ╨┤╨╛╨▓╨╛╨┤╨║╨░ ╨│╤А╨░╨▓╨╕╨╛╨║╨╛╨╜╤Ж╨╡╨╜╤В╤А╨░╤В╨╛╨▓, gravity concentrate cleaning, upgrading of gravity gold concentrate)

nodes.name: Exhauster Fan
nodes.definition: A fan or blower that extracts flue gases or vapours from process equipment, maintaining negative pressure. In the Berengela segregationтАСroasting furnace, an exhauster removes excess gases above the recirculating stream to the stack.
nodes.text: Exhauster Fan (╤Н╨║╤Б╨│╨░╤Г╤Б╤В╨╡╤А, induction fan, exhaust fan for roasting gases)

nodes.name: Gold-Antimony Ore
nodes.definition: A refractory ore containing gold together with antimony minerals, requiring combined processing methods such as flotation, roasting, and cyanidation.

nodes.name: Diesel Oil
nodes.definition: A petroleum-derived hydrocarbon fraction used as a flotation frother and auxiliary collector, particularly in telluride gold ore flotation (e.g., Emperor plant). It acts as a hydrophobic bridging agent for fine particles.

nodes.name: Ethyl Xanthate
nodes.definition: Low-molecular xanthate collector used in sulfide flotation. In the slice, it is one of the reagents tested alone and in combination with dithiophosphate, where mixtures improved galena recovery relative to the single reagent.

nodes.name: Reichert Cone Separator
nodes.definition: Gravity concentration device consisting of a series of stacked, concentric cones through which slurry flows. It separates particles by density using centrifugal and film-flow forces, commonly used for gold and heavy-mineral recovery from ground ores.

nodes.name: Trommel
nodes.definition: A rotating cylindrical screen used for washing and size classification of ore. On the Portovelo plant, it had dimensions 0.9 m ├Ч 2.4 m with 6 mm and 32 mm perforations and a slope of 1:4.2.

nodes.name: Filter Press
nodes.definition: Pressure filtration unit used to clarify cyanide solutions and to dewater gold-zinc precipitates. It produces a dense cake and clear filtrate, supporting solution recovery and downstream handling.

nodes.name: Antimony Recovery
nodes.definition: Process KPI representing the fraction of antimony transferred from ore to cathode antimony product. In the Sarylah pilot plant, overall recovery reached 96.1 % (98 % leaching, 98 % electrolysis).

nodes.name: Hillgrove Mill
nodes.definition: Antimony-gold processing plant in Australia, referenced in the context of thiocarbamide leaching technology.

nodes.name: Hillgrove Thiocarbamide Plant
nodes.definition: Industrial plant at the Hillgrove antimony-gold mine (Australia) that treats 8 t/day of concentrate (60% Sb, 30-40 g/t Au) with thiocarbamide leaching for 15 minutes. Gold is recovered from solutions by activated carbon sorption, and the de-golded antimony concentrate is sold.

nodes.name: Complex Processing of Gold-Antimony Ores
nodes.definition: An integrated processing approach combining gravity, flotation, leaching, and smelting to recover gold, antimony, and other valuable components.

nodes.definition: A hydrometallurgical pretreatment in which gold-antimony concentrates are treated with a solution of sodium sulfide and sodium hydroxide to selectively dissolve antimony minerals, leaving a gold-bearing residue for subsequent cyanidation.

nodes.name: Magnetic Separation
nodes.definition: Separation method that exploits differences in magnetic susceptibility of ore components. The slice mentions it as a common pre-flotation operation in gold-bearing ore preparation, used together with crushing, grinding, and classification.

nodes.name: Mechanical Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: Flotation machine in which an impeller mechanically sucks in and disperses air into the pulp. The slice identifies this as one of the principal machine classes and notes that it typically produces fine bubbles under optimal frother dosage.

nodes.name: Silver Concentrate
nodes.definition: A flotation concentrate rich in silver minerals, often containing tetrahedrite, argentite, or native silver. It may be processed by hydrometallurgical methods (e.g., caustic leaching) to extract antimony and recover silver.

nodes.name: Lead Concentrate
nodes.definition: A flotation product enriched in lead minerals, typically containing galena and associated silver. It is sent to a lead smelter for recovery of lead, silver, and other metals.

nodes.name: Isopropyl Xanthate
nodes.definition: A branched-chain xanthate collector mentioned in the slice as being stronger than the corresponding normal propyl xanthate in some cases. It illustrates how chain branching can improve collector action by more effectively disrupting hydrated surface layers near the mineral surface.

nodes.name: Isoamyl Xanthate
nodes.definition: A higher-chain xanthate collector used for flotation of sulfide minerals. It has stronger hydrophobizing action than ethyl or propyl xanthates and is applied in selective copper and zinc circuits.

nodes.name: Annual Silver Production
nodes.definition: The mass of silver produced in the final product per calendar year. At the Rio Tinto plant, annual silver production was 27 tonnes.

nodes.name: Three-Stage Crushing
nodes.definition: A comminution flowsheet in which ore passes through three successive crushing stages (typically jaw, cone, and short-head cone or roll crushers) to reduce particle size before grinding. It is common in gold ore preparation for downstream beneficiation.

nodes.name: Grinding in Cyanide Solution
nodes.definition: A hydrometallurgical intensification method in which ore is ground in the presence of cyanide solution rather than in water. This initiates gold and silver leaching during comminution, shortens overall cyanidation residence time, allows efficient recycling of barren solutions, and can reduce total cyanide consumption.

nodes.name: Rake Classifier
nodes.definition: A mechanical classifier in which settled sands are raked up an inclined trough for discharge. It is used in closed-circuit grinding operations for size classification.

nodes.name: Frame Clarifier
nodes.definition: A pressure filtration device composed of rectangular frames covered with filter cloth, used to remove fine suspended solids from cyanide solutions before MerrillтАСCrowe precipitation. It produces a clear filtrate suitable for zinc dust cementation.

nodes.name: Mercury Vapor Toxicity
nodes.definition: A safety and environmental constraint associated with the handling and thermal distillation of mercury-containing amalgams. Toxic vapor emissions require closed equipment, controlled heating, and strict exposure limits in order to avoid occupational poisoning and environmental release.

nodes.name: Resin-in-Leach (RIL)
nodes.definition: A combined hydrometallurgical process in which cyanide leaching of gold and silver is carried out simultaneously with ion-exchange sorption of the dissolved metals from the pulp. It is applied to carbonaceous ores to reduce metal losses due to sorption by natural carbonaceous matter.

nodes.name: Sorption Pachuca Tank
nodes.definition: A tall, conicalтАСbottomed pneumatic agitation tank specifically designed for ionтАСexchange sorption from cyanide pulps. It is used to contact the pulp with resin beads while maintaining suspension and aeration. At the Karamkenskaya plant, sorption pachucas have a diameter of 3.5тАпm, height of 16.5тАпm, and working volume of 100тАпm┬│, and are arranged in series for countercurrent resinтАСpulp contact.

nodes.name: Kidd Creek Processing Plant
nodes.definition: A Canadian copper-zinc-silver processing plant in Ontario that treats complex ores containing precious metals. In the context of carbonaceous gold ore processing, it is mentioned as a plant where flotation concentrates are smelted on copper smelters.

nodes.name: Jigging
nodes.definition: A gravity separation method in which a pulsating water flow stratifies particles by density and size on a screen or bed. Heavier grains move downward and are recovered as concentrate, while lighter grains report to tailings.

nodes.name: Gold Purity
nodes.definition: Mass fraction of gold in a refined cathodic product or bullion. In gold electrorefining it is a primary quality indicator, and the slice reports cathodic gold of about 999.8тАУ999.9 fineness.

nodes.name: Express Technological Assessment Methodology
nodes.definition: A methodology developed by Irgiredmet for the rapid and low-cost assessment of gold and silver ores. It involves calculations, chemical-mineralogical analyses, and lab experiments to assign an ore to its Technological Variety, propose a processing scheme, and forecast extraction recoveries.

nodes.name: Technological Classification of Gold and Silver Ores
nodes.definition: A system developed by Irgiredmet for classifying gold and silver ores based on their response to cyanidation. Ores are divided into Technological Classes (TC), Technological Types (TT), and Technological Varieties (TV), with the variety being the main unit. Criteria include the relative value of gold and other valuable metals, and the nature and degree of process refractoriness.

nodes.name: Relative Value of Gold in Ore
nodes.definition: A criterion for technological classification that assesses the economic contribution of gold compared to other valuable non-ferrous metals present in the ore. This determines which metal is the primary target and defines the Technological Class.

nodes.name: Degree of Technological Refractoriness
nodes.definition: A criterion for technological classification that quantifies the difficulty of extracting gold and silver from an ore using conventional cyanidation. It determines the Technological Type and Variety, guiding the choice of treatment method (e.g., direct cyanidation or pretreatment like roasting).

nodes.definition: The basic technological pathway proposed for a specific Technological Variety of ore, including potential sub-variants for optimization. It serves as the conceptual design for the beneficiation process.

nodes.name: Forecasted Gold and Silver Recovery
nodes.definition: An estimated KPI for the percentage of gold and silver that can be extracted from an ore into a final marketable product, based on the application of a standard processing scheme to a specific Technological Variety. It is used for preliminary economic evaluations.

nodes.name: Carbonaceous Arsenopyrite Concentrate
nodes.definition: A refractory gold-bearing concentrate containing arsenopyrite (FeAsS), carbonaceous matter, and pyrite, with high organic carbon content that causes preg-robbing during cyanidation. It requires combined pretreatment (roasting, pressure leaching, or mechanochemical activation) to liberate gold.

nodes.name: Gold-Antimony Concentrate
nodes.definition: A flotation concentrate containing both gold and antimony sulfides (mainly stibnite), which is refractory to direct cyanidation and often requires oxidative roasting or hot sodium sulfide leaching to liberate gold.

nodes.name: Thiobacillus ferrooxidans
nodes.definition: Iron- and sulfur-oxidizing bacterium used as a bioleaching agent in sulfide concentrate processing. It accelerates oxidation of sulfides, ferrous iron, and elemental sulfur, enabling low-temperature hydrometallurgical opening of refractory gold feeds.

nodes.name: Auriferous Pyrite
nodes.definition: Pyrite containing dispersed gold inclusions or gold-bearing surface phases. In the slice, auriferous pyrite is important because flotation after cyanidation can recover gold associated with this sulfide mineral.

nodes.name: Biohydrometallurgical Technology
nodes.definition: A processing technology that uses microorganisms for the extraction of gold and silver from refractory ores, cited as a major research direction of the Irgiredmet institute.

nodes.name: Biooxidation
nodes.definition: A pretreatment step in which sulfide minerals in refractory gold ores or concentrates are oxidized by microorganisms to expose gold surfaces for cyanide leaching.

nodes.name: Sorption
nodes.definition: Uptake of dissolved substances by a solid or liquid phase through adsorption and/or absorption. In the slice, sorption is the umbrella process behind ion-exchange resin and activated-carbon recovery of precious metals from cyanide solutions.

nodes.name: Pyrite Biodepression
nodes.definition: The selective inhibition of pyrite flotation by using thiophilic bacteria that preferentially adhere to pyrite surfaces, rendering them hydrophilic and thereby depressing their floatability while allowing coal or other valuables to float. This technique is used in coal desulfurization and sulfide separation.
nodes.text: Pyrite Biodepression (bacterial depression of pyrite, microbial pyrite depression, thiophilic bacteria for pyrite depression)

nodes.name: Mineralogical-Petrographic Composition
nodes.definition: The mineralogical and petrographic makeup of a coal or ore feed, including the relative proportions of mineral matter and petrographic constituents. In the slice, it is a key factor controlling flotation behavior together with surface oxidation and gangue inclusion characteristics.

nodes.name: Wastewater Treatment
nodes.definition: Industrial and municipal treatment domain focused on removing suspended solids, microorganisms, and dissolved contaminants from effluents. Flotation is used there as a clarification and separation method.
